openings.claim: A provenance-linked common-unit ledger may resolve discrepancies that conversion and revision tracking separately leave bounded.
openings.delta: Change the dependency between the conversion view (A) and revision register (B): carry original row identifiers through normalization and let only explicit supersession links select replacement quantities. Preserve every duplicate and unmatched row. Equal normalized quantities alone cannot establish that the older report already contains a replacement under another identifier.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: independent conversion and revision checks provide merely additive benefit. Coupling predicts positive interaction in correct resolved-batch counts, R(intact)-R(A)-R(B)+R(baseline)>0, and fewer correct resolutions when the interface is broken. Unsupported definite claims must not increase. These are proposed observations, not measured effects; the supplied awkward case may remain unresolved.
openings.probe: Propose one script producing five frozen views of identical records: baseline retaining raw rows; A alone applying only the supplied U-to-V factor; B alone registering explicit replacements without conversion; intact A×B; and link-broken A×B retaining both parent contents but withholding the row-ID interface between their outputs. Apply each to clean and disturbed copies. Freeze twelve-batch outputs with citations and at most three field-specific requests, then open the sealed key. Compare resolved counts, unsupported claims and request counts within the supplied extra twenty minutes. Record setup and maintenance time, including amendment-link repair and undefined-status handling. Keep the actual review within sixty minutes.
assumptions: Actual record contents and script setup time are not supplied; five-view construction and comparison capacity remain unverified.
A missing supersession reference or undefined status yields explicit bounded disagreement and, if prioritized, a request naming that field; never infer quantities from neighboring batches.

Defeat coupling if the interaction is nonpositive, breaking the interface does not reduce correctness, or benefits require unsupported identity matching. If setup or comparison cannot fit the stated budgets, the probe is infeasible; do not extend them.

assessment: One unmeasured coupling hypothesis. Explicit provenance, preserved rows and bounded disagreement protect the valued outcome; timing and informative comparison feasibility require verification.
